questions.question: Define responsive design and explain its importance in Android apps.
questions.solution_html:
• Define responsive design and explain its importance in Android apps.
  • Definition - (2 marks)
  • Responsive design means designing an application interface so that it automatically adjusts to
  • different screen sizes, resolutions, and orientations such as phones, tablets, and foldable devices.
  • Importance - (2 marks)
  • Importance in Android apps:
  • ● Android devices come in many screen sizes
  • ● Ensures consistent user experience everywhere
  • ● Improves readability and usability
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the role of search patterns in improving user experience in mobile apps.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the role of search patterns in improving user experience in mobile apps.
  • Definition – (2 marks)
  • Search patterns are design structures used in mobile apps to help users find information or
  • features quickly using elements like search bars, filters, voice search, and suggestions.
  • They guide users in locating content efficiently without navigating multiple screens.
  • Importance – (2 marks)
  • ● Saves user time by quickly showing relevant information
  • ● Enhances navigation, especially in content-heavy apps (e-commerce, social media)
  • ● Reduces user frustration and improves satisfaction
  • ● Increases accessibility and usability
  • ● Helps users discover features or content they didn't know existed
  • Example – (1 mark)
  • Example: In Amazon app, the top search bar with filters and suggestions helps users quickly
  • find products without browsing categories.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the difference between low-fidelity and high-fidelity prototypes.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the difference between low-fidelity and high-fidelity prototypes.
  • Definition – (2 marks)
  • ● Low-fidelity prototype: A basic, rough visual sketch of an interface showing layout and
  • concept without detailed design or interactivity.
  • ● High-fidelity prototype: A detailed, polished, and interactive version of the interface
  • closely resembling the final app design.
  • Difference – (2 marks)
  • Low-Fidelity Prototype High-Fidelity Prototype
  • Rough sketches / wireframes Polished UI with colors, fonts, icons
  • Low detail, low interaction Fully interactive and realistic
  • Used in early idea stage Used for advanced testing & client demos
  • Quick to create Time-consuming to build
  • Example – (1 mark)
  • Example: A paper sketch of app screens is low-fi, while an interactive Figma design with real
  • buttons and transitions is high-fi.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Why are visual design elements (colors, typography, icons) important in mobile UI?
questions.solution_html:
• Why are visual design elements (colors, typography, icons) important in mobile UI?
  • Definition – (2 marks)
  • Visual design elements like colors, typography, and icons create the look & feel of a mobile UI.
  • They help users understand information, improve usability, and enhance the app experience.
  • Importance – (2 marks)
  • ● Colors guide attention and communicate meaning (e.g., red for error, green for success)
  • ● Typography improves readability and hierarchy of text
  • ● Icons visually represent actions and reduce text usage
  • ● Improves visual consistency and brand identity
  • Example – (1 mark)
  • Example: WhatsApp uses green theme, simple Rybo font, and familiar icons like chat, call,
  • camera for easy navigation.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What are some fundamental UI design rules that ensure a user-friendly mobile app interface?
questions.solution_html:
• What are some fundamental UI design rules that ensure a user-friendly app interface?
  • Definition – (2 marks)
  • UI design rules are guidelines that ensure an app interface is simple, usable, and easy for users
  • to interact with.
  • Key Rules – (2 marks)
  • ● Keep interface clean and simple
  • ● Use consistent colors and icons
  • ● Ensure readable text and proper spacing
  • ● Provide easy navigation and clear buttons
  • ● Maintain visual hierarchy (headings > sub-headings > body text)
  • Example – (1 mark)
  • Example: Google apps follow Material Design — clean UI, consistent buttons, and readable
  • fonts.

questions.question: Evaluate the role of transparency and overlays in SVG graphics for modern web interfaces. How can overlay techniques impact performance, accessibility, and aesthetic appeal? [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Evaluate the role of transparency and overlays in SVG graphics for modern web
  • interfaces. How can overlay techniques impact performance, accessibility and aesthetic
  • appeal?
  • Definition – (2 marks)
  • Transparency and overlays in SVG graphics allow UI elements to appear partially see-through.
  • They help layer content visually, create depth, highlight focus areas, and improve interface
  • aesthetics. Overlays are often used for pop-ups, menus, cards, tooltips, and media controls.
  • Explanation of Role – (4 marks)
  • ● Improve focus on content by dimming the background (e.g., modal pop-ups)
  • ● Create depth & hierarchy (frosted glass, blur, shadow overlays)
  • ● Enhance readability when text is placed over images (dark layer behind text)
  • ● Used in modern UI trends like glass-morphism, blurred backgrounds, and hero banners
  • Impact on Aesthetic Appeal – (1 marks)
  • ● Makes UI modern, clean, premium-looking
  • ● Adds smooth transitions and visual depth
  • ● Creates soft, elegant visual separation instead of harsh blocks
  • Example: Apple’s iOS uses blurred glass overlays for control center and menus.
  • Impact on Performance – (1 mark)
  • ● Heavy transparency, blur filters, or multiple SVG layers can increase GPU load
  • ● May affect scrolling and animation smoothness on low-end devices
  • ● Solution: use light opacity layers or PNG fallback for older devices
  • Impact on Accessibility – (1 mark)
  • ● Overlays must maintain contrast so text remains readable
  • ● Should not hide essential content without user control (e.g., ESC to close)
  • ● Screen readers must detect and focus on overlay content
  • ● Poorly designed transparency can confuse visually-impaired users
  • Example: Netflix uses a dark overlay on thumbnails to keep text readable.
  • Example – (1 mark)
  • Example: A login pop-up in a shopping app dims the background with a semi-transparent
  • overlay so the form stays in clear focus, improving usability and creating a premium look.
